_about: Drafted by Claude on 2026-11-24 (E3, prompt 74); approved by Nav on 2026-11-24 (prompt 75). The Mars to Ceres leg's detours for the daily vote (the faster and steady options are shared, in content/vote-options.json). hours: how much later the arrival. Every fact checked against 'source' on 2026-11-24; 'quote' is the supporting text.

detours.label: Look for an asteroid with its own little moon: about 2 hours later
detours.fact: More than 150 asteroids are known to have small moons of their own.
detours.quote: More than 150 asteroids are known to have small companion moons.

detours.label: Count the asteroids around us: about 1 hour later
detours.fact: The main belt is thought to hold between 1.1 and 1.9 million asteroids more than 1 km across.
detours.quote: The belt is estimated to contain between 1.1 and 1.9 million asteroids larger than 1 kilometer (0.6 miles) in diameter

detours.label: Weigh up the whole asteroid belt: about 1 hour later
detours.fact: All the asteroids put together have less mass than Earth's Moon.
detours.quote: The total mass of all the asteroids combined is less than that of Earth's Moon.

detours.label: Study how Dawn's ion engines flew this way: about 2 hours later
detours.fact: Dawn's ion engines pushed xenon out 7 to 10 times faster than chemical rockets do.
detours.quote: accelerate ions from xenon fuel to a speed 7-10 times that of chemical engines

detours.label: Scan Ceres's high latitudes for ice: about 3 hours later
detours.fact: Dawn's measurements point to plenty of ice at Ceres's high latitudes, towards its poles.
detours.quote: indicate abundant ice at high latitudes

detours.label: Map Ceres's gravity as we close in: about 2 hours later
detours.fact: Ceres gets denser the deeper you go: its rock settled into a mantle under a water-rich crust.
detours.quote: internal density increases with depth … The rock settled to form an internal mantle overlain by the water-rich crust.

detours.label: Look out towards Jupiter: about 1 hour later
detours.fact: Young Jupiter's gravity put an end to new planets forming in the asteroid belt.
detours.quote: the gravity of newly formed Jupiter brought an end to the formation of planetary bodies in this region

detours.label: Photograph an ancient asteroid: about 2 hours later
detours.fact: Asteroids are rocky, airless leftovers from when the Solar System formed, about 4.6 billion years ago.
detours.quote: rocky, airless remnants left over from the early formation of our solar system about 4.6 billion years ago

detours.label: Test Ceres for a magnetic field: about 1 hour later
detours.fact: Scientists don't think Ceres has a magnetosphere.
detours.quote: Scientists don't think Ceres has a magnetosphere.

detours.label: Sniff for water vapour around Ceres: about 3 hours later
detours.fact: In 2012 and 2013, the Herschel space observatory found evidence of water vapour on Ceres.
detours.quote: scientists using the Herschel Space Observatory in 2012 and 2013 found evidence for water vapor on Ceres.
